I've added the flag switch to the receipt send path, but **the new receipt email itself isn't in the repo yet**. There's no template directory, no second receipt template, and no branch with one. So the flag currently points at a template name I chose, `receipt_v2`.

**What changed** (in `services/notifier/notifier/email.py`):
- `send_receipt` now checks the environment variable `NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_V2`. If it equals `"1"`, it renders `receipt_v2`; otherwise it renders the existing `receipt` template, so behaviour is unchanged by default.
- I used an environment variable rather than `flags.is_on()` / `flags.toml` because the notifier is deployed separately and can't read the root `flags.toml`. Notifier flags are named `NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>`.
- `tests/test_email.py` covers three cases: flag off (old template), flag set to `"1"` (new template), and flag set to `"true"` (still the old template, since only `"1"` turns it on). All 3 tests pass. I haven't committed anything.

**Before turning it on:**
- **Add the template:** put `receipt_v2.mjml` in `services/notifier/templates/`, with a plain-text twin `receipt_v2.txt` using the same variables (`invoice_id`, `total_minor`). If the new email already exists somewhere under another name, tell me and I'll point the flag at it.
- **Rendering isn't built:** `render()` in `notifier/render.py` currently just raises `NotImplementedError`, for both the old and new templates.
- **"Gradually" can only mean per deployment:** the flag is a single on/off switch for the whole deployed function, so you can turn it on in staging before production. It can't send the new email to, say, 10% of customers. If you want a percentage rollout, I can add a bucket based on a hash of the customer id, using something like `NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_V2_PERCENT`.
